claims.text: Traditional instruction tuning forces language models to answer questions beyond their parametric knowledge, which contributes to factual hallucinations.
Refusal-Aware Instruction Tuning (R-Tuning) measures the knowledge gap between a pre-trained model and instruction tuning data to construct datasets appended with certainty expressions.
In a multi-task setting across five in-domain datasets, R-Tuning with LLaMA-13B achieves an average Average Precision (AP) score of 76.03%, compared to 71.71% for vanilla instruction tuning.
R-Tuning generalizes refusal capabilities to out-of-domain tasks, achieving an AP score of 80.36% on HaluEval-QA using LLaMA-13B compared to 75.73% for vanilla instruction tuning.
Learning data uncertainty during instruction training yields lower Expected Calibration Error (ECE) than applying uncertainty filtering post-hoc on test data.
R-Tuning achieves refusal rates of 95.90% on FalseQA and 98.17% on NEC with LLaMA-13B, whereas vanilla instruction tuning refusal rates on these benchmarks are 6.00% and 2.36% respectively.
R-Tuning-U uses response entropy across multiple sampled model outputs to measure parametric knowledge gaps without requiring ground-truth labels for uncertain questions.

evidence.description: Previous instruction tuning methods force the model to complete a sentence regardless of whether it knows the knowledge, causing it to guess and hallucinate when faced with questions beyond its parametric boundary.

R-Tuning identifies uncertain data instances by comparing predictions against labels, constructs datasets D0 and D1 using 'I am unsure' and 'I am sure' expressions, and fine-tunes the LLM using cross-entropy loss.

Multi-task evaluation results in Table 13 show average AP scores across five datasets for OpenLLaMA-3B (61.09% vs 58.24%), LLaMA-7B (69.11% vs 68.94%), and LLaMA-13B (76.03% vs 71.71%) favoring R-Tuning over Vanilla.

Table 13 demonstrates that on the unseen HaluEval-QA dataset, R-Tuning obtains higher AP scores across all model sizes (OpenLLaMA-3B: 73.85%, LLaMA-7B: 77.17%, LLaMA-13B: 80.36%) compared to Vanilla (72.11%, 76.22%, 75.73%).
Table 16 demonstrates that R-Tuning-U achieves substantially lower ECE values across ParaRel and MMLU (e.g., LLaMA-13B ParaRel ID ECE of 0.064 for R-Tuning-U versus 0.228 for Vanilla-C).
Table 3 reports refusal rates on unanswerable question datasets FalseQA, NEC, and SA, showing R-Tuning reaches 87.32%-99.18% refusal rates while Vanilla remains between 0.96% and 34.79%.
Section 5.1 describes R-Tuning-U querying the model k=10 times at temperature 0.7, computing entropy over predictions to rank questions, and assigning the 50% most uncertain to set D0.

methodologies.name: Refusal-Aware Instruction Tuning (R-Tuning)
methodologies.description: A framework that splits instruction tuning data into certain and uncertain sets based on pre-trained model knowledge, appends uncertainty prompts, and fine-tunes models to output confidence expressions alongside answers.

methodologies.name: R-Tuning-U
methodologies.description: An unsupervised variant of R-Tuning that measures parametric knowledge boundaries by computing prediction entropy across multiple generations per question.

limitations.text: Standard instruction tuning methods force models to generate full answers regardless of parametric knowledge, causing hallucinations on out-of-knowledge questions.
R-Tuning only produces binary confidence expressions ('I am sure' and 'I am unsure') rather than continuous quantitative verbalized confidence scores.
Knowledge gap estimation relies on answer checking and uncertainty quantification rather than directly linking instruction tuning datasets to pre-training corpora.

future_work.text: Generating quantitative values to verbally express model confidence for questions rather than binary expressions.
Exploring optimization methods for entity linking instruction tuning datasets with pre-training datasets to identify relevant parametric knowledge efficiently.
